title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Driscoll clashed with Hegseth over purged generals as Iran strikes flare again.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Tuesday, September 01, 2026 — one story worth your full attention today, plus 7 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll Resigns After Rift With Hegseth
stories.why_important: The Army just lost its top civilian leader during a live conflict with Iran. Driscoll and Defense Secretary Hegseth had clashed for months over Hegseth's push to cut top generals. The Army now has a leadership gap at a dangerous moment.
stories.what_overlooked: Most reports lean on one Wall Street Journal story. The White House has not confirmed the real reason Driscoll left.
stories.prediction: Watch for Trump to name a replacement Army Secretary within days.

quick_hits.text: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths topped 1,000; nearly 4,500 people are still missing after last week's glacial floods.
US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island; Iran fired missiles and drones at Jordan and the UAE.
Kenya's aviation workers ended a strike that grounded thousands of passengers at Nairobi's main airport.
Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met in Bishkek at a Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit marking its 25th year.
Lionel Messi, 39, announced his retirement from Argentina's national team in a handwritten letter to fans.
Russian strikes killed at least 9 people in Kyiv, the sixth straight night of attacks on the capital.
The US invited Russia's Anton Siluanov back to G20 finance talks, angering European officials.

big_number.context: Venezuela's interim president gave a new US company 100-year rights to more than 17 oil fields.
